themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse Spike
themes_detail.summary: Six animal-abuse complaints filed THIS WEEK in Tottenville/Great Kills, a 500% jump versus the 8-week average of 1.0 complaint per week (z-score: 5.77), signaling a potential coordinated abuse pattern or environmental stressor affecting the district's animal population.
evidence: 6 animal-abuse complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Statistical z-score of 5.77, flagged as high severity
Sharp, sudden spike suggests possible incident cluster rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview ASPCA and local animal control; identify whether complaints cluster geographically or by abuse type
Canvass affected residents and pet owners; assess whether this reflects a single incident or multiple actors

themes_detail.label: Door/Window Break-ins
themes_detail.summary: Eight door/window complaints filed THIS WEEK in the district, a 357% spike over the 8-week baseline of 1.8 per week (z-score: 4.0), suggesting a possible uptick in residential break-ins or attempted forced entry.
evidence: 8 door/window complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Statistical z-score of 4.0, flagged as high severity
Pattern concentrated in single week suggests possible crime series or environmental factor
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with NYPD crime data and precinct reports; determine if complaints align with reported burglaries
Interview residents about timing, location, and whether break-in attempts were successful; assess need for enhanced police patrols

themes_detail.label: Standing Water & Drainage Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Three standing water complaints filed THIS WEEK in Tottenville/Great Kills, a 700% spike versus the 8-week average of 0.4 per week (z-score: 3.77), potentially linked to recent heavy precipitation or inadequate stormwater infrastructure that the CB has repeatedly requested DEP fund.
evidence: 3 standing water complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Statistical z-score of 3.77, flagged as high severity
Community Board budget request [01] for DEP capital project to develop sanitary sewers in specific street segments, repeated year-over-year, suggests chronic infrastructure gap
reporting_angles: Request DEP stormwater maps and infrastructure audit for Tottenville/Great Kills; determine which street segments lack adequate drainage
Interview affected residents about flooding frequency and property damage; cross-reference with CB budget requests to show long-unmet infrastructure need

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Three park rules violation complaints filed LAST WEEK in the district, a 1100% spike over the 8-week baseline of 0.2 per week (z-score: 6.35)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset—suggesting either a single major incident, organized misuse, or enforcement change at a specific park.
evidence: 3 park rules violation complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Highest statistical z-score in dataset (6.35), flagged as high severity
Arden Heights Woods Stream Restoration (BMP AH-2) currently in public review, may indicate park access or usage tensions
reporting_angles: Identify which parks generated the three complaints; interview Parks Dept. and community members about what violations occurred
Determine whether spike relates to Arden Heights restoration project or unrelated park misuse; assess resident sentiment around park access

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions & Illegal Dumping
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints peaked at 16 THREE WEEKS AGO (161% above the 6.1 weekly average, z-score: 3.58), and residential disposal complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK (135% above the 4.2 weekly average, z-score: 3.51), reflecting a 4-week elevated sanitation pattern that aligns with the CB's repeated requests for stronger illegal dumping enforcement.
evidence: 16 unsanitary condition complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 6.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.58); 10 residential disposal complaints filed last week vs. 4.2 weekly average (z-score: 3.51)
Community Board budget request [01] for increased enforcement of illegal dumping laws, repeated year-over-year, indicates chronic, unresolved problem
Two distinct sanitation complaint types spiking simultaneously suggests systemic waste management failure, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Map hotspots of unsanitary and disposal complaints; identify whether dumping is concentrated in industrial, residential, or waterfront areas
Interview Department of Sanitation and NYPD about enforcement capacity and illegal dumping prevention; assess whether CB's funding request has been denied or delayed
